appearance.languageHint: The language Chip Hippo's own menus, panels and dialogs are shown in. The user guide is only available in English.
appearance.fontSizeHint: The size of text in Chip Hippo's own toolbars, panels and dialogs, in pixels. Part and board markings on the desk belong to the circuit, so they scale with the desk zoom instead.
appearance.wireLayoutHint: How a new wire is drawn: Direct sags from hole to hole; Routed runs straight, and can be bent around the board by dragging points into it. Wires already on the desk keep the layout they have — change one through its own Properties dialog.

datasheets.folderHint: Point this at a folder of manufacturer datasheet PDFs named after each chip (e.g. 74LS00.pdf). When a matching PDF is found, a chip's pin-assignments window shows a button to open it.
datasheets.downloadTitle: Download datasheets into the app's own folder
datasheets.autoHint: Downloads a datasheet for every part Chip Hippo has a published source on file for — the manufacturer's own document where there is one, otherwise a reference library — into Chip Hippo's own folder, and points the setting above at it. Parts with no source are skipped, and files already there are replaced.

ai.noSecureStore: This system has no secure credential store, so a key cannot be saved. Point the base URL at a local server that needs no key.
ai.hint: Chip Hippo uses your own connection — nothing is sent anywhere until you ask it to build something, and the key is stored encrypted by the operating system, never in settings.json. Leave Base URL and Model blank to use the shown defaults.
ai.experimental: AI generation is experimental. Every design is verified against the simulator before it is offered, but it may not be the most optimal circuit or the tidiest layout — expect to review and adjust it.

warn.floatingLead: {base} ({id}) pin {pin}{suffix} is floating — its lead is over no hole.
warn.noPower: {ref} ({id}) has no {pins} connection — it will not power up.
warn.singleMember: Net "{name}" connects to only one point — a likely-forgotten connection.

review.noSupply: There is no power supply on the desk, so nothing can run. Add one from the parts tray and wire it to the board's power rails.
review.unpowered: {ref} ({id}) is wired but never reaches a supply — its VCC/GND nets carry no power.

outputsDisabledUnwired.one: {chip} drives nothing: its active-low output enable {pin} is not wired at all, and an unwired input reads HIGH. Tie it to GND.
outputsDisabledUnwired.other: {chip} drives nothing: its active-low output enables {pin} are not wired at all, and an unwired input reads HIGH. Tie them to GND.

outputsDisabledHigh.one: {chip} is switched off right now: its active-low output enable {pin} is HIGH, so its outputs float. Drive it LOW to enable them.
outputsDisabledHigh.other: {chip} is switched off right now: its active-low output enables {pin} are HIGH, so its outputs float. Drive them LOW to enable them.

review.inputFloating: {ref} ({id}) has inputs nothing drives: {pins}. A floating TTL input reads HIGH, so the chip works — just not as designed. Tie each one to VCC or GND, or wire it to whatever should drive it.
review.busFight: {drivers} are wired to the same net ({net}). Two outputs must never share a net — one drives HIGH while the other drives LOW and they fight.
review.ledUnlimited: {ref} ({id}) is conducting with nothing limiting the current — on a real bench it would burn out rather than light. Put a resistor in series with it.
